item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:

SSPDF soldiers were wounded in an assault on a Mundri West military outpost and the U.S. Embassy condemned an assault on WFP workers in Jonglei that involved looting of aid. An AIC cleric was shot dead in Juba and a Juba High Court sentenced five officers to 24 years for raiding a general's home. SPLA-IO forces retook Akobo after a deadly dawn clash. item.title: Cameroon: the situation
item.description:
Armed clashes have spread from the Northwest and Southwest to Yaounde, Douala and Maroua as security forces confront Ambazonian separatists, while separatist attacks persist in the Anglophone regions ten years after the crisis began. UNESCO has joined national efforts to prevent femicide in Cameroon. Metal Shark is constructing patrol boats for Cameroon, indicating a focus on maritime security. The Cameroon Senate President publicly denied social media rumours of an assassination attempt against him. The conflict recorded 231 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Central African Republic: the situation
item.description:
Armed clashes continue in Bangui as government forces, former Séléka rebels and Anti-balaka militias fight, with Russian Wagner forces and Africa Corps protecting President Touadéra. A large-scale militant attack was foiled, showing rebel capacity to plan major operations. Humanitarian aid deliveries are increasingly insecure, putting assistance at risk. France and Chad are meeting to rebuild defence ties, with President Macron and Mahamat Idriss Déby discussing cooperation that could affect regional security. The conflict caused 246 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Cabo Delgado, Mozambique: the situation
item.description:
Mozambique's president has set a December deadline for civilians to surrender illegal firearms, expanding the crackdown on weapons used by insurgents in Cabo Delgado. Security forces killed another member of the Anamola group in the province. Forces linked to Erik Prince suffered a battlefield loss in Congo, with a former UFC fighter among the wounded, indicating the conflict's spillover. Three Mozambicans were repatriated after being victims of human trafficking. The insurgency caused 151 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Myanmar's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The junta carried out a drone strike that damaged a Chinese gas pipeline facility, while Chinese courts sentenced three Myanmar scam gang members to death. Drone attacks hit Naga villages in Myanmar, prompting condemnation from NSF and NSCN-IM. The military continued its shadow banking expansion, hosted a delegation in Sri Lanka, and intensified airstrikes on a historic Buddhist meditation centre, a monastery, villages in Sagaing and displacement camps in Rakhine, killing civilians. The conflict caused 2,332 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Hezbollah explosives seized in two Lebanese trucks have prompted Lebanon's prime minister and security forces to promise a thorough investigation, while Israeli artillery and air strikes continue against Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon, causing civilian casualties. In northern Israel, a Hezbollah submunition exploded in a teenager's backpack during a hike near the Lebanon border, killing Elazar Yair Wilensky and wounding dozens, leading the IDF chief to order a probe and authorities to consider restricting hikes. Students on the same hike fashioned tourniquets from belts and socks after the blast. Hezbollah announced compensation for Lebanese homeowners whose houses were destroyed and unveiled an aid plan for displaced civilians. The UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.title: Libya: the situation
item.description:
A covert operation seized a Lockerbie bombing suspect on Libyan territory, showing continued security actions against international terrorism. Khalifa Haftar’s son met the Inspector General of Morocco’s Royal Armed Forces and later met Syria’s foreign minister in Libya, linking Libyan factions to regional actors. Over 130 migrants died when a boat capsized off the African coast, and mines under fire contest gold control in the Egypt-Sudan-Libya border triangle. The government warned of penalties for unauthorized protests, and there were two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
